The setup typically looks like this: ``` gh pr checkout xxx # xxx is the PR number # update code git add . git commit -m 'foo' git push ``` This workflow has been working correctly over the past 6 months but recently, I get stuck at `git push` and get ``` error: Authentication error: Authentication required: You must have push access to verify locks error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/contributor/fork.git' ``` Yet, when I run `gh auth status -h github.com` things look ok. On the one hand, this seems sensible in view of the [github doc]( https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/committing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork), that states: > You can only make commits on pull request branches that: [...] have permission granted from the pull request creator On the other hand, the PRs have a "Maintainers are allowed to edit this pull request." check (see screenshot below). ## Question Is this a bug? Has there been any recent change that may be responsible for that?
